sections.h2: What should I know before selling fast in East Windsor?
sections.html:
Match the method to your deadline. East Windsor owners can work with an agent, go it alone, or take a cash offer, and the best fit depends on condition, tenants and timing. The township adds a step of its own: a fire prevention check of smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and an extinguisher before a single-family home or condominium is sold.

East Windsor's population was estimated at 30,562 in mid-2025, compared with 30,045 in 2020 and 27,190 in 2010. Owners live in about 61 percent of the homes, and tenants in the rest.

  • Working with an agent: reaches financed buyers, and takes the longest.
  • Going it alone: you handle price, contract and the township check yourself.
  • Cash sale as-is: helps with postponed repairs, a vacant property, or a hard deadline.

sections.h2: What is the East Windsor township sale inspection?
sections.html:
The Bureau of Fire Prevention checks smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and the fire extinguisher before a sale. The township's Selling Your Home page gives the steps: complete the Fire Inspection Form, then deliver or mail it with a $50 check or money order payable to East Windsor Township. Cards are refused, and the township asks for a week to process. A call follows to set the inspection, held mornings on varying days.

The resulting certificate lasts 60 days, so fix a closing date before booking. The inspector reviews how well the detectors work and how old they are, the extinguisher, the record of work and site conditions. Smoke detectors may be no older than 10 years and carbon monoxide detectors no older than 7, going by the manufacturer's label. A 2A10BC extinguisher with this year's tag must be in the kitchen, though it need not be mounted. Failing means repeating the process and paying a $25 re-inspection fee.

The township answers at 609-443-4000, extension 406, from the Municipal Building at 16 Lanning Boulevard.

sections.h2: Does East Windsor require a Certificate of Occupancy at resale?
sections.html:
The township's Certificate of Occupancy page names three residential triggers: new construction, additions, and reconstruction after fire, storm or vehicle damage. A plain resale does not appear among them. The Construction Department also issues continued certificates and certificates of approval, so ask whether anything applies to your property, particularly if a reconstruction job never received a final sign-off.

For a rented house, the construction page sends owners to the East Windsor Health Department at extension 416 for lead-based paint inspections in rental dwellings.

sections.h2: Where is East Windsor and what surrounds it?
sections.html:
In Mercer County, East Windsor covers 15.57 square miles where the Delaware Valley meets the Raritan Valley, an outer-ring New York suburb that also touches the Philadelphia metro area. Its neighbors are Robbinsville and West Windsor in Mercer, Cranbury, Monroe and Plainsboro in Middlesex, and Millstone and Upper Freehold in Monmouth. The independent borough of Hightstown sits wholly inside East Windsor, making the pair one of 21 doughnut towns in New Jersey.

Windsor Township divided on February 9, 1797, producing East and West Windsor, and East Windsor was incorporated on February 21, 1798. Growth arrived late: 2,298 residents in 1960, then 11,736 in 1970 and 21,041 in 1980. Twin Rivers, home to 7,878 people in 2020, was described in a state guide as New Jersey's first planned unit development. If your home is in Twin Rivers, ask the community association what paperwork it expects at resale.

sections.h2: How good is East Windsor's access to highways and transit?
sections.html:
Several major highways meet here. Turnpike Exit 8 is inside the township and feeds Route 33 and Route 133, the Hightstown Bypass. U.S. Route 130 crosses the western part, with county routes 535 and 539 adding local links. Of roughly 93 miles of road, 69 belong to the municipality.

Suburban Transit's 300 line goes to Port Authority in Midtown and its 600 line to Wall Street. The nearest NJ Transit rail stop is Princeton Junction, with a rush-hour shuttle, and Mercer County runs a shuttle along Route 130. Hospitals within reach include Penn Medicine Princeton Medical Center, about 7 miles away in Plainsboro, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital's Hamilton division, about 10 miles, and CentraState in Freehold, about 17 miles. The average commute is 26.8 minutes.

sections.h2: What jobs and schools are tied to East Windsor?
sections.html:
The township has a pharmaceutical cluster. Hovione, CoreTech, Aprecia, Sabinsa, Novotec, Aurobindo and Windsor Labs all have sites there, and Route 130 carries much of the retail. Freehold Raceway Mall, Quaker Bridge Mall and Princeton Market Fair are short drives.

The East Windsor Regional School District serves East Windsor and Hightstown with six schools and 5,138 students in 2022-23. Walter C. Black and Ethel McKnight cover kindergarten through grade 2, Perry L. Drew and Grace N. Rogers cover grades 3 to 5, Melvin H. Kreps Middle School takes grades 6 to 8, and Hightstown High School takes grades 9 to 12. Eighth graders anywhere in Mercer County can apply to Mercer County Technical Schools, which charge no tuition.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about East Windsor housing?
sections.html:
For 2020 through 2024, the middle owned home is valued at $397,400 and median household income is $105,208. About 45 percent of adults 25 and older hold at least a bachelor's degree, and roughly 44 percent of residents use another language at home.

sections.h2: What will an East Windsor seller pay, and where does the deed go?
sections.html:
The state realty transfer fee is the seller's. Using $397,400, the Census middle value for owned homes in East Windsor, the state schedule gives about $3,190. Mercer County's Clerk page adds that the graduated charge on sales of $1 million and up, starting at 1 percent, moved to the seller as of July 10, 2025.

  • Township check: $50 with the Fire Inspection Form, plus $25 if a second visit is needed.
  • Filing the deed: the Mercer County Clerk charges $43 for a regular deed's first page and $10 for every added page.
  • How to pay: transfer fees go in by cash, cashier's check, money order, attorney trust account or business escrow account, with certified or bank checks required above $10,000.
  • State form: a GIT/REP seller certification accompanies the deed.

The Records Room welcomes the public on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30, and the Indexing Section's number is 609-989-6476.

faqs.q: Is a fire inspection required to sell in East Windsor?
faqs.a: Yes for a single-family home or condominium. The Bureau of Fire Prevention certifies detectors and an extinguisher before the sale, at $50, with a certificate good for 60 days.

faqs.q: What detector ages does East Windsor accept?
faqs.a: Smoke detectors up to 10 years old and carbon monoxide detectors up to 7, per the manufacturer's label. The kitchen also needs a 2A10BC extinguisher with a current-year tag.

faqs.q: What if the East Windsor inspector fails my house?
faqs.a: Fix the items and run the process again with a $25 re-inspection fee. The certificate expires after 60 days, so book early enough to leave room for a second visit.

faqs.q: Will a resale in East Windsor require a Certificate of Occupancy?
faqs.a: The township's residential list covers new construction, additions and reconstruction. If your house was rebuilt after a fire or storm, ask Code Enforcement whether a final certificate was issued.

faqs.q: Who files an East Windsor deed?
faqs.a: The Mercer County Clerk. A regular deed runs $43 for page one and $10 for each page after, and the transfer fee has to arrive by an accepted method such as cash, cashier's check, money order or attorney trust account.
